channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan's First Lady Addresses UN General Assembly on Global Issues
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration of Uzbekistan, spoke at the 81st UN General Assembly. She outlined Uzbekistan's stance on international security, trust-building, and regional changes in Central Asia, emphasizing openness, good neighborliness, and dialogue.

item.title: Taliban Administration Spends Over 45% of Budget on Security, World Bank Reports
item.description: Security spending by the Taliban administration accounted for over 45% of its total expenditure in the current fiscal year, according to a World Bank report. This spending reached 51.3 billion afghanis, or approximately $787 million, exceeding combined spending on education, health, and infrastructure.

item.title: Uzbekistan court sentences Taftish.uz staff and former security officers
item.description: A military court in Uzbekistan has sentenced staff from the Taftish.uz editorial office and former National Security Service (DXX) officers. Editorial head Ghayrat Aberayev received 10 years and 6 months, journalist Marjona Eshquvvatova 4 years and 1 month. Others received sentences over 10 years for charges including defamation and fraud.

item.title: China-Uzbekistan trade fair opens in Tashkent, boosting regional logistics
item.description: A "China-Uzbekistan-2026" international trade fair has opened in Tashkent. The event aims to expand trade and logistics, with China's ambassador highlighting the potential of the China-Europe freight train. Cooperation prospects include infrastructure, new energy, agriculture, and technological innovation.

item.title: Kazakhstan declares September 25 a national day of mourning after military incident
item.description: Kazakhstan has declared September 25 a national day of mourning following an incident during Caspian Sea exercises. A sharp deterioration in weather conditions led to 19 military personnel being washed away, with the death toll now reaching 12.

item.title: Kandahar Bombing Injures Eight, Kills Seven at Mirwais Hospital
item.description: Seven people killed and eight injured in a Kandahar bombing were transferred to Mirwais Hospital. Sources report the injured were construction workers and some are in critical condition. The bombing occurred early Thursday morning in the Sarai Mullah Sahib area.

item.title: Head of Supreme Shia Council Released from Taliban Justice Minister's Custody
item.description: Local sources report that Mohammad Ali Ekhlaqi, head of the Supreme Shia Council, was released from the personal prison of the Taliban's Justice Minister. He and another council member were reportedly tortured and forced to pledge no further political activity.

item.title: US and Iran Negotiate Phased Deal to End War, Reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description: US and Iranian negotiators are exploring a phased approach to end the ongoing war. The proposed deal involves Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz for shipping in exchange for the US lifting its economic blockade and releasing frozen assets.

item.title: Uzbekistan Expands Tourism Cooperation Within CIS Framework
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing tourism cooperation with CIS countries. Meetings in Dushanbe included discussions on expanding tourist exchanges, developing regional and cross-border tourism, and jointly promoting Central Asia. Kazakhstan was invited to the Tashkent International Tourism Fair.

item.title: Taliban Claims Attack on Pakistani Border Post in Kandahar
item.description: The Taliban's 'Al-Badr 205 Corps' claims to have attacked a Pakistani border post in the Spin Boldak district of Kandahar. A spokesperson stated a Pakistani border post was destroyed and significant casualties inflicted. Pakistani officials have not commented.

item.title: Rising Suicide Figures in Afghanistan Raise Concerns
item.description: Multiple reports of suicide incidents from different Afghan provinces in a single day highlight a worrying trend. The true extent of the phenomenon is unknown due to difficulties in recording and reporting cases, but recurring media reports suggest the issue requires serious attention.

item.title: Afghanistan's Empty Seat at UN General Assembly Highlights International Isolation
item.description: For five years, Afghanistan has lacked presidential representation at the UN General Assembly, signaling its diminished standing. The Taliban regime's restrictions on women, exclusion of societal groups, and disregard for international concerns have deepened the rift with the global community.

item.title: Taliban Extort Ghazni Residents Over Alleged Weapon Possession
item.description: Taliban forces in Afghanistan's Ghazni province have allegedly extorted money from residents of Nawur district under the pretext of possessing weapons. Four individuals were reportedly tortured and forced to pay for their release, with others given a week to provide weapons or equivalent cash.

item.title: Turkey Agrees to Return Military Base in Northern Iraq to Baghdad
item.description: Following negotiations in New York, Turkey and Baghdad have agreed to gradually hand over the Bashiqa-Zelikan base near Mosul to the Iraqi government. Both sides also reached an agreement to halt the activities of illegal foreign armed groups and Kurdish militants in the region.

item.title: Discussion on Fresh Pakistani Airstrikes on Afghanistan
item.description: This news item focuses on a discussion regarding recent Pakistani airstrikes on Afghanistan. It also includes related news snippets about Afghanistan's participation in the Asian Games cricket, Pakistan's claims about attackers' roots, the OIC meeting on Afghanistan, and regional conflicts involving Iran and the US.

item.title: Uzbekistan Food Safety Committee Head Meets Entrepreneurs
item.description: Azizbek Urunov, head of Uzbekistan's Food Safety Committee, met with food production, processing, and export entrepreneurs. Discussions covered a presidential decree on unified state management and control in food safety, phytosanitary, and veterinary spheres. Andijan region's significant role in the food industry was highlighted, with 9.6 trillion soums of food production in 2025.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Offers Condolences to Kazakhstan Over Military Deaths
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov expressed deep sorrow to Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev following a tragic incident that resulted in the deaths of military personnel during exercises in the Caspian Sea. Japarov conveyed condolences on behalf of the Kyrgyz people and offered support to the families of the deceased and recovery wishes to the injured.

item.title: Bishkek Mayor Inspects Construction Site of 24-Story Residential Complex
item.description: Bishkek Mayor Aybek Dzhunushaliyev met with residents and the contractor of a 24-story residential complex under construction in the city center. Residents raised concerns about construction safety, adherence to norms, and preservation of green spaces. The mayor instructed the developer to work within the allocated territory and ensure safety.

item.title: Former Interior Minister Omurbek Suvanaliyev to Run for President in 2027
item.description: Former Interior Minister Omurbek Suvanaliyev announced his intention to run for president in the 2027 elections. Suvanaliyev, a critic of the current government, believes a strong opposition candidate is needed. He aims to unite opposition forces for the upcoming presidential race. The elections are scheduled for January 27, 2027.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Iraq Discuss New Trade and Investment Projects
item.description: Uzbekistan's ambassador to Iraq, Ayubkhon Yunusov, held meetings in Baghdad to discuss trade, transport logistics, and legal frameworks. Discussions focused on expanding bilateral trade, direct business ties, and a preferential trade agreement. Both sides considered establishing Uzbek trade houses in Baghdad and Erbil and preparing for the first Joint Intergovernmental Committee meeting.

item.title: AI's Impact on Education and Future Professions Discussed at ICTWEEK Uzbekistan
item.description: A forum on AI threats in education and employment at ICTWEEK Uzbekistan 2026 explored how to prepare youth for future jobs and the skills in demand. Experts discussed AI's influence on learning and the job market. The 'AWS Academy' program was launched in 12 universities, and the 'Heirs of Muhammad al-Khwarizmi' project was announced nationwide.

item.title: Mahmoud Abbas: Israel's Gaza Violence Caused Unprecedented Humanitarian Catastrophe
item.description: Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas addressed the UN General Assembly, stating that Israel's violence in Gaza has resulted in an "unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe." He described the situation as a "genocidal war" causing killings, destruction, hunger, and displacement, impacting essential life necessities and future generations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan customs officers prevent illegal import of cars from Korea
item.description: Customs officers in Kyrgyzstan have uncovered a violation of customs legislation concerning the illegal import of vehicles from Korea. The discovery was made by the 'Northern' railway customs department's anti-smuggling unit.

item.title: Kabul students complain about high costs and poor quality of private dormitories
item.description: Students in Kabul are complaining about the high cost and poor quality of services in private dormitories. Issues include hygiene, inconsistent water and electricity, low-quality food, overcrowding, and insufficient bathrooms.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Gavi Strengthen Partnership for Sustainable Immunization System
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Health Minister Damir Osmonov met with Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, in New York. The meeting focused on country leadership, sustainable financing, and improving healthcare systems. Gavi's contribution to Kyrgyzstan's immunization system, including new vaccines, was highlighted.

item.title: World Food Programme Urges UN to Address Afghanistan's Hunger Crisis
item.description: The World Food Programme (WFP) is calling on the UN General Assembly to not forget the ongoing crisis in Afghanistan. The organization highlighted the severe hunger and malnutrition affecting families, particularly mothers and children seeking assistance at nutrition clinics.

item.title: Afghanistan Freedom Front Claims Taliban Member Killed in Kabul Attack
item.description: The Afghanistan Freedom Front reported that one Taliban member was killed and two others injured during an attack on a patrol vehicle in Kabul. The group stated its forces sustained no casualties in the incident, which occurred on Wednesday evening in the Dasht-e Barchi district.

item.title: Iranian Plane Forced to Return to Tehran Due to US Sanctions
item.description: An Iranian airline flight en route to Dushanbe, Tajikistan, was compelled to return to Tehran after Turkmenistan denied it airspace access. This incident follows the implementation of new US sanctions against Iranian aviation companies.

item.title: Afghan Hazara leader warns Taliban against ethnic persecution
item.description: Mohammad Karim Khalili, leader of the Islamic Unity Party of Afghanistan, warned the Taliban that they cannot eradicate the Hazara people, just as Abdul Rahman Khan failed. He cited ongoing discrimination, confiscation of religious and economic centers, and property seizures against Hazaras.

item.title: ADB forecasts Tajikistan's economy to grow 7% in 2026
item.description: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) projects Tajikistan's economy to grow by 7% in 2026 and 6.5% in 2027. Inflation is expected to be 4.5% in 2026 and 4.7% in 2027. The previous forecast for 2025 was 8.4% growth.

item.title: Tajikistan's industrial production grew by 13.8% in January-August 2026
item.description: Tajikistan's industrial production increased by 13.8% in January-August 2026, reaching 45.37 billion somoni. Manufacturing saw a 23% rise, while energy and water supply sectors grew by 19.3% and 17.2% respectively. Investment in fixed assets nearly doubled.

item.title: New 'Keskanyor' border post to open between Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A new border post named 'Keskanyor' will be established on the border between Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has tasked officials with developing the project and commencing construction within three months.

item.title: Tajikistan and Russia agree on mutual recognition of customs control results
item.description: Tajikistan and Russia signed a protocol on the mutual recognition of electronic customs control results during a CIS customs services meeting in Belarus. The agreement aims to enhance customs cooperation, expand digital technologies, and simplify procedures.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev Addresses Poverty and Unemployment in Andijan
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev expressed concern about poverty, unemployment, and migration in the Andijan region. He questioned how he could remain at ease in Tashkent knowing these issues. The statement highlights the administration's focus on regional socio-economic challenges.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Open New Border Post 'Keskanyor' with Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to open the 'Keskanyor' border post, twice the size of 'Dostlik', with Kyrgyzstan. An agreement has been reached, with project development and construction to begin within three months. This aims to triple cargo volume and halve transit times. Additionally, construction of a paid Tashkent-Andijan highway is slated to start in 2027.

item.title: Tajikistan and China to Expand Cooperation in Science and Technology
item.description: Tajikistan and China held a working meeting to discuss scientific and technological cooperation, including joint initiatives within the 'One Belt, One Road' and SCO frameworks. Key areas include water resources, ecology, climate change, and digital technologies. Both sides explored possibilities for joint research projects and academic exchanges.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces 500,000 Soum Subsidy Per Ton for Cotton Sold on Exchange
item.description: Uzbekistan will provide a 500,000 soum subsidy per ton for cotton sold on the exchange, benefiting both farmers and clusters. An additional 1.5 million soum subsidy per hectare will be given to clusters growing cotton on their own land. Support for exporters and development of fruit and vegetable processing are also planned.

item.title: Former Bishkek Deputy Mayor Azamat Kadyrov Detained Until November 20
item.description: Former Bishkek Deputy Mayor Azamat Kadyrov has been remanded in custody until November 20. He was responsible for land use, architecture, construction, and digitalization. The specific charges against him are not yet known. Kadyrov served as deputy mayor since November 2023.

item.title: New 'Keskaner' Border Crossing to Appear Between Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A new border crossing, 'Keskaner,' twice the size of the current 'Dustlik,' will be established between Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan. This is expected to triple cargo traffic and reduce border crossing times. The project is linked to increased transport flows, including the planned China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway.

item.title: China and Russia Account for Over Half of Kyrgyzstan's Trade Turnover
item.description: In January-July 2026, Kyrgyzstan's foreign trade turnover exceeded $10 billion. China and Russia remain the main economic partners, accounting for over 60% of total trade. Exports grew significantly in July, driven by precious metals and textiles, with Russia being the largest buyer.
